Subject: Request: invoicing cadence aligned to semiannual fiscal windows

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is enthusiastic about Redwood's latency profile and the dedicated capacity option. Procurement asked me to follow up with a billing request tied to our fiscal calendar.

Short version: Stonebridge runs semiannual budgeting for vendor payments (two main disbursements: Apr 1 and Oct 1). They asked whether Redwood will accept a semiannual invoicing cadence (two invoices per 12 months) with Net-90 payment terms measured from the invoice date. In practice that means we would submit one invoice covering Apr–Sep and one for Oct–Mar, with payment due 90 days after each invoice.

I realize this is nonstandard and could have cashflow implications. Procurement is prepared to provide a single irrevocable PO per year and a corporate guarantee letter, and they'd accept a modest contract amendment (invoice schedule + PO ref). Attached is a one-page memo from Finance that explains their process.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is something you can sign off at the enterprise level, and whether any commercial conditions (e.g., fee uplift, deposit, or credit hold) would be required?

Appreciate a quick read — we need an answer by end of week to keep our procurement window open.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of IT Procurement
Stonebridge Health

Marissa / Aditya — looping you both in. Prospect asks for semiannual invoicing + Net-90. Deal summary below (short):
- Account: Stonebridge Health (target ARR: $1.2M)
- Requested terms: 2 invoices/year (Apr & Oct), Net-90 from invoice date
- Customer offers: single irrevocable annual PO + guarantee letter
- Timeline: needs decision by Friday (7/9) to meet their procurement cycle

Why this matters: this deviates from Redwood standard monthly/quarterly invoicing and shifts working capital burden to us (could be 6 months revenue outstanding). Given the size of the deal, a concession may be worth it, but we should define compensating controls (e.g., fee uplift, deposit, or contractual payment triggers).

Proposed internal ask: 1) Sales exec approval for a one-year pilot of semiannual cadence on this account, conditional on finance/legal-approved mitigations; 2) If approved, Marissa to negotiate commercial tradeoffs (upfront deposit or 3–5% MSR uplift); 3) Aditya to confirm acceptable credit terms / required documents (PO, guarantee, ACH mandate).

I attached the procurement memo Liam provided for context.

Naomi

Thanks Naomi — reviewed the memo and ran a quick impact calc (attached). Key points:
- Revenue at risk: ~6 months of invoiced services outstanding per cycle (~$600k cash tie-up)
- Margin impact if we add uplift: a 3% uplift offsets ~half the financing carry cost; a 5% uplift brings us near neutral assuming a 60-day cost of capital.
- Alternatives: require a 25% deposit at contract signature OR accept semiannual invoicing conditioned on a signed annual irrevocable PO + ACH debit authorization + auto-renew clause for consecutive years.

Given the strategic fit (potential for expansion into their clinical AI pilots) I would recommend conditional approval with one of the compensating controls above. If we go the deposit route, we should offer a 3% discount on annual commitment as a concession (keeps headline price attractive).

Requesting exec-level approval: Markus, can you confirm whether Finance has latitude to accept this pilot with the proposed controls, or whether we need to escalate to COO/CFO?

Thanks,

Team,

Short answer: conditional approval from Finance for a time-limited pilot, subject to the following non-negotiables:
1) Stonebridge provides an annual irrevocable PO on company letterhead (signed).
2) Stonebridge sets up an ACH debit mandate or approves an auto-debit clause that triggers on invoice due date (Net-90).
3) Redwood requires either a 20% deposit at contract signature OR a 3% commercial uplift across invoiced amounts.
4) Legal to include explicit payment schedule and remedy language (late interest, suspension rights) in the Master Services Agreement; Legal to review final redline.

If Sales is comfortable with those controls, Finance will approve a one-year pilot limited to this account. Anything less and we must require full prepayment.

Markus — please confirm if you want to elevate to COO/CFO for an exception approval or if I should proceed with preparing the conditional term sheet for Liam / Stonebridge.
